def:joint-packet.title: Finite source-complete joint packet
def:joint-packet.note: Encoded. RepresentedJointPacket (Lambda, V, M, E) bundles the represented data (J1)-(J5) in the coordinates of the central type decomposition: the common carrier is Carrier = Sigma lambda, (Fin 4 x V lambda) x M lambda (the paper's H_X up to the unitary decomposition of (J3), which the structure fixes as coordinates); (J1) the faithfully represented external Clifford factor A_Cl = M_4(C) acts as extAction a = blockDiagonal' (a (x) I (x) I), a unital *-representation (extAction_mul/one/conjTranspose) faithful when some sector is nonempty (extAction_injective); (J2)/(J3) the kinematic typing algebra A_type = ⊕ I_4 (x) B(V_lambda) (x) I_M is intAlgebra = range intAction (mem_intAlgebra_iff), commuting with A_ext (extAction_commute_intAction); (J4) the directed incidence graph is (src, tgt : E -> Lambda) with represented incidence operators Y e : C^4 (x) V_{s e} (x) M_{s e} -> C^4 (x) V_{t e} (x) M_{t e}, placed on the (t e, s e) corner of the carrier by incidenceOp (blockEmbed); (J5) the mixed words are the elements of actionAlgebra = jointActionAlgebra A_ext A_int Y (def:action-algebra), star-closed; multiplicityAlgebra = its commutant. No inverse incidence map is a field. The earlier duality-facing SourceCompleteJointDualityPacket remains the packet used by thm:SMST-main-duality; linking the two (proving the commutant identities for a RepresentedJointPacket) is thm:main-duality, not this definition. Re-verified 30 Sep 2026 against the renamed statement (A_ext -> A_Cl, A_int -> A_type, incidence histories -> incidence operators, mixed history words -> mixed represented products on the same carrier): the change is terminological, the encoded fields are unchanged.

def:action-algebra.title: Joint typed action algebra
def:action-algebra.note: Statement encoded (new version renames the generators: A_act = C*(A_Cl, A_type, Y_e, Y_e^*) instead of C*(A_ext, A_int, ...)). jointActionAlgebra A_Cl A_type Y : Subalgebra C (Matrix n n C) is starAdjoin (the least star-closed unital subalgebra = the finite-dimensional C*-algebra generated) of A_Cl ∪ A_type ∪ range Y with the incidences Y_e represented as matrices on the common carrier; the two generating sets are arbitrary parameters, so the encoding is unchanged by the renaming. Editorial change only (the remark that 'action' means represented operator action, not the variational functional, is prose).

thm:trinity.title: Factor obstruction and typed decomposition
thm:trinity.note: Assembled across several theorems. New first clause (the former thm:factor-obstruction): matrix_representation_normal_form gives, for a unital copy phi : M_n(C) -> M_N(C), N = n k and an invertible conjugator with phi(a) ~ a (x) I_k (H = C^n (x) K, K = C^k); smst_factor_obstruction / smst_factor_obstruction_exact give M_n(C)' = {g (x) 1}' = 1 (x) M_K exactly, its factoriality, and the nontrivial-centre obstruction (a set containing a non-scalar central element is not that commutant), i.e. a reducible algebra with nontrivial centre cannot be the full commutant of the external factor. Typed decomposition: matrixBlockDecomposition gives A_type as a product of full matrix blocks; finite_commutant_decomposition supplies for every unital star-closed algebra the central block projectors, star matrix units, carrier unitary decomposition and the mutual-commutant identity (arbitrary finite Lambda); the explicit displayed Kronecker forms C = (+) B(C^n (x) V) (x) I and C' = (+) I (x) B(M) are proved literally only for two sectors (commutant_decomposition, block_bicommutant). def:incidence-coefficients.title: Intrinsic incidence coefficient space
def:incidence-coefficients.note: Encoded (the file was written for the earlier def:multiplicity-quiver, which this definition generalizes to arbitrary represented edges). For a block T : (V_b x N_b) x (V_a x N_a) matrix (the paper's Y_e : K_lambda (x) M_lambda -> K_mu (x) M_mu with K = V, M = N), functionalSlice phi T = (phi (x) id)(T) for phi in B(V_a, V_b)^*, sliceSpace = {(phi (x) id)(T_j)} and arrowSpace = its span = the paper's B_e (eq:intrinsic-incidence-coefficients, 'a linear operator space, not a single residue'); arrowSpace_eq_span_blockSlice is eq:general-incidence-expansion for the matrix-unit Hilbert-Schmidt basis (the coefficients F_{e,a} of any other HS orthonormal basis are functional slices along its dual functionals, so their span is the same arrowSpace; not displayed separately). def:typed-multiplicity.title: Typed multiplicity algebra
def:typed-multiplicity.note: Encoded for a represented joint packet P (RepresentedJointPacket, def:joint-packet) with incidences Y_e : K_{s(e)} x M_{s(e)} -> K_{t(e)} x M_{t(e)}, K_lambda = C^4 x V_lambda. (i) def:incidence-coefficients: the intrinsic coefficient space B_e = {(phi (x) id)(Y_e) : phi in B(K_s, K_t)^*} is coefficientSpace P e, the range of the slice map phi |-> (phi (x) id)(Y_e) (sliceLinearMap, linear in phi), hence a linear operator space and not a single residue; mem_coefficientSpace_iff is literally the set of eq:intrinsic-incidence-coefficients and coefficientSpace_eq_span_blockSlice is eq:general-incidence-expansion (B_e = span of the HS-basis coefficient blocks F_{e,a}). (ii) eq:typed-multiplicity: M_type = typedMultiplicityAlgebra P, the StarSubalgebra of Pi_lambda Matrix (M lambda) (M lambda) C cut out by R_mu B = B R_lambda and R_lambda B^H = B^H R_mu for EVERY B in B_e and every edge e (IsTypedMultiplicity; closure under +, *, 1, scalars, star proved); isTypedMultiplicity_iff_blockSlice reduces the quantifier over B_e to the finitely many coefficient-block equations. As a star-closed unital subalgebra of a finite-dimensional matrix algebra it is a unital C*-algebra on the total multiplicity carrier. (iii) iota((R_lambda)) = (+)_lambda I_{K_lambda} (x) R_lambda on the full carrier Sigma lambda, (Fin 4 x V lambda) x M lambda is multiplicityAction (multiplicative, unital, star-preserving, faithful when every V_lambda is nonempty). (iv) eq:coefficient-action-algebra: O_Y = C*(Z_lambda, B, B^* : B in B_e, e in E) on the total multiplicity carrier Sigma lambda, M lambda is coefficientActionAlgebra P := StarAlgebra.adjoin of the vertex projections Z_lambda (vertexProjection) and the corner-embedded slices blockEmbed B; it contains the generators and their adjoints and coefficientActionAlgebra_le_iff states it is the least star-closed unital subalgebra containing them (in finite dimension the algebraic star hull is the C*-hull). thm:main-duality.title: Arbitrary-incidence action--multiplicity reconstruction

(ii) eq:coefficient-quiver-duality O_Y'_M = M_type and M_type'_M = O_Y on the total multiplicity carrier (coefficientActionAlgebra_commutant / coefficientCarrierAlgebra_commutant), and M_type = End Q_Y for the adjoint-closed coefficient quiver (typedMultiplicity_iff_quiverEnd: forward arrows Y_e and adjoint arrows Y_e^*, arrow spaces = spans of all functional slices; this clause is stated with Lambda, E : Type because MultiplicityQuiverArrows.QuiverEnd is). Scoping/disclosure: the packet is given in the coordinates of its central type decomposition (as in RepresentedJointPacket: the paper only requires unitary equivalence to the displayed sum); iota is faithful when every V_l is nonempty (iotaTypedMultiplicity_faithful), so iota(M_type) is a faithful copy of M_type exactly in the paper's situation (V_l = representation spaces). prop:incidence-slice-Gram.title: Slice Gram and operator--Schmidt spectrum
prop:incidence-slice-Gram.note: Proved (incidence_slice_Gram assembles). Y in B(K_s,K_t) (x) B(M_s,M_t) is a matrix Y : Matrix (K_t x M_t) (K_s x M_s) C. Both operator spaces carry their HS products; in the HS-orthonormal matrix-unit coordinates (vecEquiv) the slice map S_Y is the realignment matrix realign Y and its HS adjoint is the conjugate transpose; vec_functionalSlice_hsFunctional proves S_Y(conj D) = (phi_D (x) id)(Y) with phi_D(A) = Tr(D^* A) (hsFunctional), and H_Y := sliceGram Y = realign Y * (realign Y)^H. Clauses: H_Y PSD (sliceGram_posSemidef); eq:incidence-slice-Gram-range Ran H_Y = Ran S_Y (range_sliceGram_eq_range_realign, via rank(AA^H) = rank A) = B_Y (range_realign_eq_sliceSpace, B_Y = {(phi (x) id)(Y) : phi} the intrinsic slice space, every functional being some phi_D); rank H_Y = dim B_Y in general; Tr H_Y = ||Y||_HS^2 for every Y (trace_sliceGram). eq:incidence-slice-Gram-spectrum for an operator-Schmidt decomposition Y = sum_k sigma_k D_k (x) F_k with HS-orthonormal (D_k), (F_k) (finite index type, r = card) and real sigma_k: H_Y F_k = sigma_k^2 F_k (sliceGram_mulVec_schmidt), rank H_Y = r when all sigma_k != 0 (rank_sliceGram_schmidt; Schmidt coefficients are positive), Tr H_Y = sum sigma_k^2 (trace_sliceGram_schmidt). Rendering disclosed: operators on the HS spaces are represented by their matrices in the matrix-unit orthonormal bases.

thm:support-polar.title: Exact support-polar duality
thm:support-polar.note: Proved on the general finite multi-vertex incidence graph (SimpleGraph G on a finite vertex type, oriented edge data F h : Matrix (M v) (M u) C arbitrary: rectangular, singular, rank-deficient or zero), on the total multiplicity carrier TotalCarrier M = Sigma v, M v of SupportPolarActionAlgebra.lean with the official supportPolarAlgebra (def:support-polar). thm:incidence-polymatroid.title: Incidence rank polymatroid

thm:geometry-short.title: Universal geometry short and active residual
thm:geometry-short.note: Proved. eq:geometry-short-general: the pseudo-inverse Schur short equals S_int^*(I - P_ST) S_int and is PSD (sourceSchurResidual_eq_orthogonalResidual, _posSemidef). eq:geometry-short-quotient: dim(E / Ker G) = rank G (finrank_minimalCarrier_short). eq:geometry-short: with the accepted Gram theta I and vanishing mixed block the short is theta I_12 (active_product_short_eq; the hypotheses 'scalar accepted Gram, additional spacetime scores orthogonal to the accepted source' of the explicit orthogonal active realization are taken as hypotheses, exactly as the paper's proof uses them; the realization's construction layer itself is not encoded). eq:residual-S4 (residual_S4_census): the five orthogonal Hermitian central projectors Qtype, QW2, QC, QG, QP of ActiveResidualAlgebra (traces 1,2,3,3,3, summing to one, each block irreducible: every corner Q X Q lies in the represented S_4 x <iota> algebra) carry, for every sigma in S_4, the characters 1, chi_{V_2} = fixMatch - 1 (three perfect matchings), chi_W = fix - 1, chi_W, sgn * chi_W, and the reversal acts by +1 on the first three and -1 on the last two: this identifies them with C_type^+, (V_2)_+, W_+, W_-, (W x sgn)_- (a finite-dimensional representation being determined by its character); the five S_4 x <iota> characters are pairwise distinct (blockChar_injective), so the endpoint module W_- and the loop module (W x sgn)_- are distinct. thm:active-isotypic.title: Complete census, colour eligibility, and flat termination

(3) Private-line census (2,2,1,1) at the level of characters and NEW eq:degree-one-private-commutant: PrivateLineWedderburn.privateLineCommutantEquiv : M_2(C) x M_2(C) x C x C ~=_alg privateLineCommutant (the relative commutant of PmPlus sigma = Pm sigma (+) 1 on E (+) C), dimension 10 (finrank_privateLineCommutant). The map sends (N, M, b, c) to the block matrix [[N00 Qtype + M00 QC + M01 E12 + M10 E21 + M11 QG + b QW2 + c QP, N01 u0], [N10 v0, N11]] with u0 the constant column and v0 = (1/12) u0^H (Qtype = (1/12) J by Z1_eq, kernel-checked); injectivity by the explicit block/trace coordinates coords', surjectivity by splitting X in the commutant into blocks, using degreeOneCommutantEquiv for the E-block and the invariant-vector lemmas column_invariant / row_invariant (S_4-invariant columns and rows on the ordered roots are constant, from transitivity act_transitive of the relabeling action, kernel-checked). (4) Neither algebra contains a unital copy of M_3(C) (degree_one_colour_no_go). prop:ten-panel-reconstruction.title: Explicit ten-panel reconstruction
prop:ten-panel-reconstruction.note: Proved in the paper's concrete frame: accepted operators A_{e,a} = K_e ⊗ Q_a (TenPanel.acceptedOp), Gram M_ϑ = ϑI + (1−ϑ)cc* (coefficientGram) with the explicit positive square root √ϑ(I−P) + √h P identified with Mathlib's CFC.sqrt (cfc_sqrt_coefficientGram), frame coefficients C_ν = Σ_j (M_ϑ^{1/2})_{jν} A_j, Stinespring map V = Σ C_ν ⊗ |ν⟩, Heisenberg pullback 𝒫*(F) = V*(I⊗F)V, and eq:complementary-pullback 𝒫*(|z⟩⟨w|) = C(z)*C(w) proved for any finite coefficient family (complementaryPullback_vecMulVec). ten_panel_reconstruction gives both boxed formulas D_μ ⊗ I = (2√3/√(ϑh))(𝖷_μ + i𝖸_μ) and K_e = I/√18 + Σ_μ O_{eμ} D_μ; the manuscript's intermediate claims C(u) = √(h/12) I and C(r_μ) = (√ϑ/2) D_μ ⊗ I are the lemmas pulledCoefficient_uniformEnv / pulledCoefficient_contrastEnv; the 'determines the represented system algebra and commutant' clause is encoded as ten_panel_determines_coefficients (equal ten pullbacks ⇒ equal coefficient families, hence equal algebra and commutant). prop:reconstruction-error.title: Robust commutant stopping test
prop:reconstruction-error.note: TenPanel.reconstruction_error proves all three clauses in the ten-panel frame: with measured panels X̂_μ, Ŷ_μ of Hilbert–Schmidt errors ε_{X,μ}, ε_{Y,μ} and the linear reconstruction D̂_μ = (2√3/√(ϑh))(X̂_μ + iŶ_μ), K̂_e = I/√18 + Σ_μ O_{eμ} D̂_μ (reconstructedCoefficient), (i) (Σ_e ‖K̂_e − K_e ⊗ I_R‖²_HS)^{1/2} ≤ e_K := (2√3/√(ϑh))(Σ_μ (ε_{X,μ}+ε_{Y,μ})²)^{1/2} (eq:appendix-reconstruction-error, via helmert_sum_norm_sq: OᵀO = I preserves the sum of squared errors); (ii) ‖(𝒟̂ − 𝒟)x‖ ≤ 2√2 e_K ‖x‖ for the star-closed stacked commutator maps jointCommutatorL2 (starClosedStack ·) (eq:appendix-commutator-error, via ‖A‖_op ≤ ‖A‖_HS and the existing jointCommutatorL2_sub_norm_le); (iii) if 𝒟̂ has least singular value ≥ ŝ on a protected complement W (ŝ‖x‖ ≤ ‖𝒟̂x‖ for x ∈ W) and ŝ > 2√2 e_K, then no nonzero x ∈ W lies in ker 𝒟 (generic versions: robust_commutant_stopping_test also gives the lower bound (ŝ − 2√2 e_K)‖x‖ ≤ ‖𝒟x‖ and the matrix form; robust_commutant_stopping_test_ker gives ker 𝒟 = M when W = Mᗮ for a verified protected M ⊆ ker 𝒟). Disclosed conventions: the reconstruction lives on the common carrier E × R, so the true coefficient compared against K̂_e is K_e ⊗ I_R (the paper writes K_e); the 'measured least singular value ŝ on the protected complement' is formalised as the bound ŝ‖x‖ ≤ ‖𝒟̂x‖ on W (equivalently ŝ ≤ σ_min(𝒟̂|_W)); hypotheses as in prop:ten-panel-reconstruction plus OᵀO = I.

thm:word-module-recognition.title: Word-module recognition of historical internal actions
thm:word-module-recognition.note: Proved, and more generally than stated: for any unital C-algebra A (no finite-dimensionality, C*-structure or Wedderburn form needed; the statement is purely algebraic) and any family of algebra automorphisms alpha : G → (A ≃ₐ[C] A) (no group structure or finiteness of G needed), on the regular word carrier W = A with L_a = LinearMap.mulLeft, R_b = LinearMap.mulRight, U_g = (alpha g).toLinearMap: word_module_recognition states R(A)' ∩ U(G)' = L(A^G) as an equality of subsets of Module.End C A (commutants are Set.centralizer, A^G = invariantElements alpha = {a | ∀ g, alpha g a = a}, which is the fixed-point form of A ∩ {u_g}' for alpha_g = Ad(u_g)); word_module_recognition_iff is the 'equivalently' clause (T commutes with every R_b and every U_g iff T is left multiplication by a unique invariant element) and word_module_recognition_coefficient gives the coefficient T 1. The Hilbert-space structure of L^2(A, tau_reg) plays no role in the theorem and is not encoded (the carrier is the underlying vector space).

prop:word-module-defect.title: Exact module and symmetry defects
prop:word-module-defect.note: Proved. Setting: A a nontrivial finite-dimensional normed star ring over C with an inner product satisfying IsRegularTraceInner (<x,y> = tau_reg(x^* y) with tau_reg(z) = D^{-1} Tr_A(L_z), the intrinsic normalized regular trace formula of normalizedRegularTrace, equal to D^{-1} sum n_beta Tr(z_beta) in Wedderburn form); symmetries U_g = alpha_g given by a group hom alpha : G ->* (A ≃ₗᵢ[C] A) with alpha_g(1) = 1 (the paper's Ad(u_g) by unitaries is a special case, since tau_reg is tracial: regularTraceForm_mul_comm). hsNorm is the Hilbert-Schmidt norm (l^2 norm of (S e_nu) over the standard orthonormal basis), proved basis-independent via LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner (hsNorm_sq_eq_sum). word_module_defect: ||T - L_{T1}||_HS = delta_R(T) (eq:word-module-defect, also squared form); groupAverage_identity: |G|^{-1} sum_g ||alpha_g a - a||^2 = 2||a - E_G a||^2; hsNorm_mulLeft_sq: ||L_b||_HS^2 = D||b||^2; word_module_invariant_defect: ||T - L_{E_G(T1)}||_HS <= delta_R(T) + sqrt(D/2) delta_G(T) (eq:word-module-invariant-defect); defects_vanish_iff: both defects vanish iff T = L_a with a G-invariant (the 'Thus' clause). cor:word-multiplicity-firewall.title: Word-space multiplicity firewall
cor:word-multiplicity-firewall.note: Proved in the scoped form recommended by the assessor: the corollary's mathematical content is witnessed on the paper's own twelve-root benchmark (Appendix prop:word-space-inflation: E = directed edges of K_4, S_4 relabeling matrices Pm, A = M_12). word_space_multiplicity_firewall: (i) the fixed points of the conjugation representation conjRep sigma X = P X P^{-1} on the word space L^2(M_12) are exactly the invariant algebra A^{S_4} = commutantSubmodule, so the trivial-representation multiplicity on the word space is finrank = 7 (commutant_finrank_eq_seven); (ii) the trivial multiplicity on the exposed physical carrier C^E is 1 (fixed vectors = constants, via S_4-transitivity on directed edges proved by decide); hence 'multiplicity on L^2(A) need not equal multiplicity on the physical carrier'; (iii) the word-space commutant contains an M_7(C) block: m7Block is an injective multiplicative linear embedding of Matrix (Fin 7) (Fin 7) C into End(L^2(M_12)) commuting with every conjRep sigma (built from the group average E_G and End(A^{S_4}) ≅ M_7); (iv) the physical invariant algebra A^{S_4} admits no injective linear image of M_3(C) (no_M3_embedding). Not formalised: the full multiplicity vectors (1,0,2,1,1) vs (7,5,19,17,12) for the non-trivial irreducibles (that is prop:word-space-inflation, a separate record) and the corollary's normative clauses ('must also pass thm:word-module-recognition', 'multiplicity-birth analysis refers to the physical carrier'), which are interpretive.

def:word-native-shadow.title: Word-native linear shadow

thm:external-shadow-no-go.title: Word moments cannot manufacture an external shadow
thm:external-shadow-no-go.note: Proved as a countermodel for an arbitrary finite old letter process K (h x Fin 2 resolved carrier, spectator two-level system, h nonempty). external_shadow_no_go packages: (i) both the even (clockZ) and odd (clockX) extensions recover every old word after normalized grading discard (conservative); (ii) the historical word algebras coincide literally (every extended old word is the same matrix), hence identical multiplication tables; (iii) the complete word-Gram hierarchies Tr(w1^H w2) coincide and equal twice the old Gram (trace_kronecker); (iv) all resolved entries of every historical word coincide (resolved cylinder data); (v) the proposed left-to-right grading cross block is 0 in the even extension and nonzero in the odd one; (vi)/(vii) no function of the historical word data, and no function of the word-Gram hierarchy, returns the cross block of both extensions. Scope: the grading-changing variant of the cross block is the instance exhibited (the theorem is existential, so one instance suffices); the typed-incidence variant is not separately modelled.

prop:word-space-inflation.title: Invariant word-space inflation without an internal $M_3$
prop:word-space-inflation.note: Proved. word_space_inflation, on the benchmark E = ordered unequal pairs of Fin 4 with the relabeling matrices Pm sigma: (1) the algebra generated by the point projections and the fibre averages T, H (Tm, Hm, entries 1/3 on same tail / same head) is M_12(C) (adjoin_gens_eq_top, via thm:connected-router: the support graph of the router T+H is connected, router_preconnected, explicit walks of length <= 3); (2) A^{S_4} = the commutant of the Pm sigma in A = M_12 (invariant_algebra_eq), which is isomorphic to C x M_2(C) x C x C (DegreeOneWedderburn.degreeOneCommutantEquiv); (3) the permutation character chi(sigma) = Tr Pm sigma (trace_Pm_eq_permChar; class values (12,2,0,0,0), permChar_classes) has character inner products (1/24) sum chi_lambda chi = (1,0,2,1,1) in the order (1, sgn, W, W x sgn, V_2) (physical_multiplicities); (4) the conjugation representation X -> P X P^{-1} on L^2(M_12) = M_E(C) has LinearMap.trace equal to chi(sigma)^2 (trace_conjRep, via Tr(X -> AXB) = Tr A Tr B, trace_mulLeft_comp_mulRight) with inner products (7,5,19,17,12) (conjugation_multiplicities); (5) its commutant contains an injective multiplicative M_7(C) block (WordSpaceFirewall.m7Block); (6) A^{S_4} admits no injective linear image of M_3(C). cor:historical-typed-compilation.title: Historical typed-compilation criterion
cor:historical-typed-compilation.note: Proved as the criterion the paper's proof establishes. A flat historical word hierarchy is a FlatWordTable: a finite word bank of the historical *-algebra A with its multiplication table w_i w_j = sum_k t_ijk w_k and flatness (the bank spans A, so represented elements and finite functional-calculus elements p(a) are bank combinations); the word Gram is G_ij = tau(w_i^* w_j) for the inner product <y,x> = tau(y^* x) (tau = tau_reg gives the Grand-Tensor Gram). Typed shadows are TableNativeShadow: word-native maps X -> sum c_a A_a X B_a (def:word-native-shadow) whose insertions are declared in the bank; compressions by represented typing projectors, finite symmetry/router averages and compositions are table native (compression, groupAverage, comp). The compiler `compile` reduces every inserted product in the table (eval_compile). historical_typed_compilation: (1) the ordinary, ordinary-shadow and shadow-shadow blocks of the complete mixed ancestry Gram equal explicit functions gramForm of the word Gram, the table and the declared data; (2) the Schur ancestry residual H - C^* G^dagger C (ancestryShort, spectral Moore-Penrose inverse, the display eq:table-native-short) equals its compiled form; (3) the alternating determinant shadow DetIncidence.alt of an incidence tensor compiled entrywise from typed Gram blocks equals its value on compiled entries. historical_typed_compilation_determined: two hierarchies on different algebras with the same table, Gram and declared data give the same Gram, residual and alternating shadow (no independent cross-Hankel row). Converse: external_shadow_not_compilable restates thm:external-shadow-no-go (no function of the word-Gram hierarchy returns the external cross block). Disclosed renderings: 'represented or functional-calculus elements' = bank combinations; the Store-Clifford and matter-incidence shadows = arbitrary table-native shadows; the incidence tensor entering the alternating shadow is taken entrywise from typed Gram blocks. Re-verified 30 Sep 2026: the new version adds that the same table computes the six naturality defects of thm:six-naturality when their amplitudes and tensor-leg actions are historical (and defers mixed branches to prop:naturality-compilation). Disclosed: this clause is an instance of the shadow-shadow block clause of historical_typed_compilation with the defect maps R_X, S_Y as TableNativeShadow (they are word-native maps X -> a X - X b when the tensor-leg actions are bank elements) and the amplitudes as bank words, so d_nat = sum of shadow-shadow Gram diagonal entries is table-compiled; no separate Lean statement names the naturality defects, and the mixed-branch pointer is not a claim of this corollary.

thm:connected-router.title: Connected-router full-matrix theorem
thm:connected-router.note: Proved on Matrix n n C for any finite index type n with decidable equality (nonempty for the direction full-algebra => connected, since Mathlib's SimpleGraph.Connected includes nonemptiness). C*(D_n,u) is encoded as the unital subalgebra Algebra.adjoin C (D_n ∪ {u, uᴴ}); the support graph is SimpleGraph.fromRel (u i j ≠ 0), and diagProj_mul_mul_diagProj_ne_zero_iff identifies the paper's edge condition p_i u p_j ≠ 0 with u i j ≠ 0. adjoin_eq_top_iff_connected is the boxed equivalence eq:router-full-matrix (walk induction single_mem_of_reachable + top_of_units); disconnected_block_reduction gives, for a disconnected support graph, a nonempty proper adjacency-closed component whose block projection commutes with the generated algebra (reducing subspace) and a proper block-diagonal subalgebra containing the generated algebra.

cor:one-router-minimality.title: One-router source minimality
cor:one-router-minimality.note: Proved with an explicit router on an n-dimensional carrier Fin n with diagonal minimal projections p_i = E_ii: the nilpotent cyclic shift N (N_{i,i+1} = 1, support graph the path 1-2-...-n) satisfies (i) StarAlgebra.adjoin C {p_i, N} = top = M_n(C) for every n (cyclicRouter_generates; matrix units built from p_i N p_{i+1} along the path, adjoints for the reverse direction, then WeakReset.top_of_units); (ii) N is nonnormal for n >= 2 (cyclicRouter_not_normal, N N^H != N^H N); (iii) the star algebra generated by any set of diagonal matrices, in particular by the p_i alone (no off-diagonal word), is commutative (diagonal_generated_commutative via Algebra.commute_of_mem_adjoin_of_forall_mem_commute). one_router_source_minimality packages (i)-(iii) for n = m + 2. Scope: the manuscript's 'cyclic nonnormal router' is instantiated by this nilpotent shift (sufficiency is an existential claim, so one router instance suffices); the general connected-router criterion is thm:connected-router, not needed here.

prop:bridge-router-residuals.title: Minimal bridge and weak-router residuals
prop:bridge-router-residuals.note: Proved. Colour: delta_col(u) = ||p_H u p_T||_HS^2 + ||p_T u p_H||_HS^2 on C^3 = T + H_priv is identified with omegaCol of InternalCommutantSeedExact; with the thm:colour-bridge generators (p_T, the four private matrix units = the hypothesis that private words generate M_2(H_priv), u, u*), the generated algebra equals the reducing block algebra M_2 + C (InternalSeed.blockDiag) iff delta_col = 0, and equals M_3 iff delta_col > 0. Weak: for p = |t><t|, q = |h><h| with unit t, h in C^2, delta_wk = ||[p,q]||_HS^2 = 2c^2(1-c^2), c = |<t,h>| (from the all-vector polynomial identity ||[p,q]||^2 = 2|<t,h>|^2 ||t||^2||h||^2 - 2|<t,h>|^4); delta_wk > 0 iff p != q and <t,h> != 0 (p = q iff c^2 = 1, via the 2D Lagrange identity |t0 h1 - t1 h0|^2 + |<t,h>|^2 = ||t||^2||h||^2), and then p, q generate M_2(C) (WeakReset.two_lines_generate). Norms are encoded entrywise (sum of |entries|^2); unit vectors as sum of normSq = 1.

thm:subdirect-classification.title: Finite subdirect matrix-algebra classification
thm:subdirect-classification.note: Proved (finite_subdirect_classification). Setting: B a unital star-closed subalgebra (Subalgebra + star_mem hypothesis) of the product ring Pi_{i<r} M_{n_i}(C), n_i >= 1, all coordinate projections surjective. Conclusion: there are k classes with sizes d_beta >= 1, a surjective class function cls : Fin r -> Fin k with n_i = d_{cls i} (coordinates in one class have equal matrix size; distinct sizes are never identified), and invertible V_i in M_{n_i}(C) such that x in B iff exists Y in Pi_beta M_{d_beta}(C) with x_i = V_i Y_{cls i} V_i^{-1} for all i (Y_{cls i} read in M_{n_i} through n_i = d_{cls i} via Matrix.reindex (finCongr _)); i.e. B is the diagonal embedding of one independent full matrix algebra per class, up to the inner automorphisms Ad(V_i). Infrastructure built: exists_wedderburn_pi_matrix (intrinsic Wedderburn decomposition B = Pi_beta M_{d_beta}(C) for any star-closed subalgebra of Pi_i M_{n_i}(C): transport along the block-diagonal embedding to FiniteComplexStarSubalgebraSemisimplicity.starSubalgebra_isSemisimpleRing, then Mathlib's IsSemisimpleRing.exists_algEquiv_pi_matrix_of_isAlgClosed), exists_factor_algEquiv_of_surjective (a surjective unital hom Pi_beta M_{d_beta} -> M_n kills all summands but one and is an isomorphism on it: images of the central units are scalar idempotents summing to 1; RingHom.injective out of the simple ring M_d), algEquiv_matrix_size_eq (isomorphic full matrix algebras have equal size), and NCG.matrix_algEquiv_inner (Skolem-Noether) for the inner form. Scoping: n_i >= 1 (paper's implicit nondegeneracy of the displayed factors); C*(B) is rendered as the unital *-closed subalgebra; 'up to inner automorphisms' is rendered with invertible (not necessarily unitary) conjugators V_i, which is what the paper's proof (Skolem-Noether) supplies.

thm:reciprocal-return.title: Finite reciprocal-return criterion
thm:reciprocal-return.note: Proved (reciprocal_return_criterion) at the paper's horizon n = dim N, for a finite group G with a unitary representation v (v(gg') = v g v g', v 1 = 1, v_g^* v_g = 1) whose commutant is scalar (Schur form of irreducibility), h self-adjoint, all index types finite, V nonempty. The declared route bank is encoded as words (lists) in the letters A_g = (v_g (x) I)A, A_g^*, B_g^* = B^*(v_g^* (x) I), B_g, D = I (x) h, and arbitrary operations inside T and inside H_priv (the represented private support words), acting on T + (V (x) N) + H_priv; a word 'has a colour bridge' when its H_priv <- T corner is nonzero (HasBridge). Established: the boxed identity m_ret = d^-1 Tr(rho_B W_A) and m_ret >= 0; (i) <=> (ii) <=> (iii) <=> (iv), where (iv) is 'rho_B h^k rho_A != 0 for some k' (all k in N, equivalently k < n by Cayley-Hamilton, partialGram_pow_mul_eq_zero_all), i.e. Ran rho_B not orthogonal to the h-cyclic space of Ran rho_A; when the conditions fail, the explicit subspace T + K + 0 with K = cap_{g,k} Ker B^*(v_g^* (x) h^k) (it contains V (x) Ran W_A) is invariant under every letter of the bank -- the letter set is closed under adjoints, so this is a reducing subspace -- contains T and is annihilated by the H_priv coordinate, so no word of the bank has a bridge; when they hold, the witness B_1^* D^k A_g has k + 2 <= n + 1 letters. Disclosed gap: the paper's reducing projection is onto T + (V (x) Ran W_A); the Lean subspace is the (possibly larger) invariant subspace of mediator vectors from which no return word reaches H_priv, which serves the same purpose.

cor:reciprocal-return-force.title: Port-relative reachability forces colour

thm:fusion-native-alignment.title: Fusion-native sufficient criterion for same-carrier alignment

thm:rectangular-normalization-kernel.title: Exact rectangular normalization kernel

prop:determinant-normalization-isolation.title: Alternating-sector isolation fixes the branch weight

A normalized instrument is a finite Kraus family with sum_b K_b^H K_b = 1 and P_alt is any nonzero idempotent matrix (the paper's I_C (x) |a><a| = T_0^H T_0 is one). branch_weight_eq_one: if the distinguished branch has effect x . thm:determinant-arity-floor.title: Sharp five-slot determinant-mode floor
thm:determinant-arity-floor.note: Formalised as weight bookkeeping on the graded basis: single-system carrier C⊕W₂⊕N (Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 2 ⊕ N, weights (1,0),(0,1),(0,0)), endWeightSupport w = {w i − w j} (the central-weight support of End), tensorWeight = slot sums on the diagonal k-fold carrier. determinant_arity_floor: support ⊆ {(0,0),±(1,0),±(0,1),±(1,−1)} (equality when N nonempty), (−3,−2) absent from the single-system support, absent on k-fold carriers for k<5 (total charge bound a,b≥0, a+b≤k), present at k=5 (line C⊗C⊗C⊗W₂⊗W₂ of weight (3,2) → neutral line). torusAction_conj_single proves that conjugating the matrix unit E_ij by the diagonal torus action diag(e^{i(aα+bβ)}) multiplies it by the character of w i − w j, so endWeightSupport is the actual central character support of the matrix units; det_weight_matrix_unit exhibits the k=5 rank-one map with character (−3,−2). No downgrade.

prop:naturality-compilation.title: Finite functional and word-moment realization
prop:naturality-compilation.note: Proved. Contextual route: trace_determined_of_mem_span shows that for H in the real span of the tested functionals F_l, Tr(F_l J) = Tr(F_l J') for all l implies Tr(H J) = Tr(H J') (span induction; J_D itself is never used, so the bank determines the functional without determining the Choi operator); naturality_defect_and_trace_determined applies it to H_nat and I giving d_nat and Tr J_D; trace_determined_modulo_constants is the refinement with H = H_0 + c, H_0 in the span and c constant on the declared feasible class. Word-moment route: with H_nat = sum_X R_X^H R_X + sum_Y S_Y^H S_Y (eq:naturality-operator) and J_D = sum_a |T_a>><<T_a| (amplitudeChoi), word_naturality_defect proves d_nat = Tr(H_nat J_D) = sum_a (sum_X ||R_X T_a||^2_HS + sum_Y ||S_Y T_a||^2_HS) (eq:word-naturality-defect). Scoped rendering: the port is a finite coordinate space p -> C (the amplitude space in Hilbert-Schmidt coordinates), the inserted actions R_X, S_Y are matrices on it, and ||.||^2_HS is the coordinate sum of normSq. The sentences 'at flatness their multiplication table computes it exactly' (thm:inserted-word-moments, already proved) and the trace-convention remarks are interpretive and not restated.

cth:zero-hypercharge-exotic.title: Hypercharge support can miss a gauge-charged exotic
cth:zero-hypercharge-exotic.note: Proved on top of the formalized inventory of thm:canonical-chiral-projectors. For any passing target packet (CanonicalChiralProjectors.Inventory with P_gch = P_SM, target weights y_f != 0 as in the SM table) on K = C^iota, extendedCarrier adjoins the pair of weak triplets on C^3 (x) C^2 (one per chirality): X'_j = X_j (+) (A_j (x) I), Y' = Y (+) 0, Gamma' = Gamma (+) (I (x) diag(+1,-1)), for any Hermitian family A_j with no common kernel (instantiated by weakAdjointFamily: the adjoint generators (J_a)_bc = -i eps_abc on three weak generator indices, Hermitian, realizing ad(sigma_a/2) on the Pauli basis (adjointGen_ad), no common kernel). zero_hypercharge_exotic: every target intertwiner space has unchanged dimension (so every linear anomaly row is unchanged) and every nonzero-hypercharge projector is P'_{f,+-} = P_{f,+-} (+) 0; every exotic chiral trace Tr(Gamma_E w) of a word in the exotic generators vanishes (opposite chiralities cancel; Y = 0 on the pair kills every abelian term); the pair lies in Ker Y'; Delta_inv^F = Tr(P_gch - P_SM) = 6 = rank(P_gch - P_SM); and rank(P_0Y - P_0) = 6 for any orthogonal projector P_0Y whose fixed vectors are Ker Y' (eq:zero-hypercharge-exotic-gap). exotic_invisible_and_charged: Y' K = 0, P_0' K = 0, P_gch' K = K. z6_acts_trivially_on_adjoint: every element of the common kernel Z_6 (prop:faithful-SM-quotient) has scalar weak component and acts trivially by g2 M g2^* (colour/abelian factors trivial by the charge assignment (1,3)_0), so the pair represents the same quotient. exists_exotic_carrier: an explicit instance (trivial passing packet + adjoint pair) with Delta_inv^F = 6. Renderings disclosed: 'passing' = Delta_inv = 0 (P_gch = P_SM) with nonzero target hypercharges; the cubic SU(2) anomaly clause is covered by the vanishing of all chiral traces of the pair.

prop:fermion-source-completeness.title: Finite certificate for completeness of the retained fermion source
prop:fermion-source-completeness.note: Proved in the paper's form. With P_K a Hermitian idempotent (P^2 = P, P^H = P) and K = Ran P_K (carrier), C_{F|K} := U^H (1 - P_K) U (completenessResidual): fermion_source_completeness bundles C = ((1-P)U)^H ((1-P)U) >= 0 (PSD); C = 0 <=> Ran U <= K (eq:fermion-source-completeness-zero, first equivalence); Ran U <= K <=> for all A in A_F, A(Ran U) <= K for any set A_F containing I and leaving K invariant (second equivalence, sourceRange_le_carrier_iff_invariant); Tr C = ||(1-P_K)U||^2_HS (completenessResidual_trace, HS norm as sum of normSq); and rank C + dim(Ran U ∩ K) = dim Ran U (completenessResidual_rank_add, by rank-nullity for (1-P)|_{Ran U} and rank(V^H V) = rank V), which is eq:fermion-source-completeness-rank. lem:complete-typed-source.title: Complete multiplicity synthesis from the saturated fermion source

lem:collective-compactness.title: Asymptotic compactness gives collective compactness
